This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226
And 227 Of Constitution Of India Praying To Declare
That The Acquisition Of Schedule A To C Properties
Vide Annex-A Dtd.20.8.1997 Have Lapsed And
Consequently Restrain The R-1 From Interfering With
The Possession Of The Schedule-A To C Properties.

This Petition Coming On For Preliminary Hearing
In 'B' Group This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Present petition seeking issuance of a declaration that the acquisition of schedule A to C properties in terms of final notification dated 20.08.1997 has lapsed and for consequential relief of injunction restraining respondent No.1 from interfering with the possession of petition schedule properties.

2. It is the contention of the petitioners that they are the legal representatives of one Sri Karagaiah,
who was the owner of schedule A and B properties and petitioner No.5 is the owner of 'C' schedule property.

It is further contended that though the said properties were the subject matter of preliminary NC: 2023:KHC:32463 notification dated 18.9.1992 and final notification dated 20.08.1997, they have remained in occupation and possession of the said properties.

In other words,
it is contended that the possession of the land has not been taken.
It is their further contention that compensation has also not been paid.
On these grounds, the present petition is filed seeking the aforesaid reliefs.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners reiterating the grounds urged in the Memorandum of Petition submits that since neither possession is taken nor compensation is paid, in law, the acquisition is deemed to have been lapsed and therefore, he submits that petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for.

sentences.text: Sri T P Vivekananda, learned counsel for the 1st respondent drawing the attention of this Court to annexure R-2 - publication of notification issued under Section 16(1) of the Act of 1894 submits that possession of the acquired land has been taken.
In that notification, petition schedule properties are reflected at Sl.Nos.86, 98, 99 and 100.

He further submits that the predecessor-in-title of the petitioners viz.,
Karagaiah NC: 2023:KHC:32463 had been issued with a notice and endorsement and even the compensation has been paid as detailed in paragraphs 4 and 5 of the statement of objections.

Thus,
he submits that the acquisition has been completed in the manner known to law and the acquired land has stood vested with the authorities free from all encumberances.

He further refers to a memo dated 30.01.2023 filed along with three copies of deeds of sale dated 10.10.2005, 15.11.2005 and 25.11.2006 and also a copy of application filed under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.

Referring to the said documents learned counsel submits that the present petitioners are not entitled to maintain this petition inasmuch as they have parted with their so called title over the petitioner schedule properties, that too after transfer in favour of third parties.

He further draws the attention of this Court to the order dated 18.04.2016 passed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.Nos.48275/2012 and connected matters to contend that the so called subsequent purchasers had approached this Court challenging the very same notification unsuccessfully and had withdrawn the said petition with liberty to avail remedies available under law, if any.
Thus referring to the aforesaid document, learned counsel for respondent No.1 NC: 2023:KHC:32463 submits that apart from the petition being not maintainable, reliefs as sought for may not be granted.

5. In response, learned counsel for the petitioners fairly submits that he would restrict his prayer in the present petition to the extent of relief for compensation and interest payable thereon and he would not press the relief of declaration of lapse of acquisition.
He further submits that though in terms of the deeds of sale, petitioners have parted with the property, there are pending litigations with regard to the right, title and interest of the petitioners.
Therefore, he submits that liberty be reserved to the petitioners in this case as well to make representation to seek relief of compensation and interest and other remedies if available in law.

6. Accepting the aforesaid submission of the petitioners and the respondent, this Court is of the considered view that petition be disposed of reserving liberty to the petitioners to make representation with the respondent/authorities to seek compensation in accordance with law.
Such representation shall be made within two weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

Upon receipt of such NC: 2023:KHC:32463 representation, if the compensation is not paid already, respondent No.1 shall consider the same in accordance with law, and dispose of with an outer limit of eight weeks from the date of receipt of representation.
Petition disposed of accordingly.
